title: Knip the Little Witch
content:
Knip was not feeling well. Aunt Ro made a potion for her to drink, but Knip didn't want it. It smelled terrible!

As Knip walked to school, she began to feel worse. She coughed and coughed!

At school, the teacher asked Knip to cast a spell on a rat.

It worked! The rat turned into a tomato.

But when Knip did her next spell, she coughed while saying the magic words.

Something went terribly wrong!

Knip tried again. But as her cough got stronger, the rabbit got stranger!

Knip's cough was out of control.

Everything was going wrong.

Then Knip's wand turned the spell on her!

Knip cried so loudly that everyone ran away.

Finally, Knip realized that she needed to take Aunt Ro's potion.

Knip's throat felt better!

Now Knip could say the magic words with ease.

Soon everyone felt better, especially Knip.

But she still needed to spend some time practicing her spells!

Copyright page

title: The Ant and the Butterfly
content:
One day, an ant was carrying a piece of bread into his house.A butterfly sitting on a leaf looked down at the ant."Hello, Ant! What are you doing? Let’s play!" said the butterfly."Hello, Butterfly! I would like to play too, but not now. The rainy season is about to start,so I must store up a lot of food," the ant answered, breathing hard.

The butterfly asked, "Ant, why do you need to work so hard? Look over there. That's my friend Grasshopper. He doesn't worry about anything. He says that we don't have to work because there's food everywhere. He sings well and makes me happy. Because of him, I don’t worry about anything."But the ant continued to work."Poor Ant; you should play more." The butterfly laughed at the ant.The ant just bowed. "I want to play too, like you, but I have to work hard now to collect food for my family to eat during the rainy season."So every day, the ant worked.One bit of bread, two bits, three bits…. He collected food, storing it in his house."One, two, three, four… Now, I only need to collect a few more. I’m so tired. But I can do it!If I work harder, my family can live happily," he said.

The butterfly continued to play and didn’t worry about anything."La la la, la la la… What a beautiful morning.Na na na, na na na… What a beautiful day," sang the butterfly happily.The butterfly sipped sweet nectar from the flowers. Then the butterfly saw the grasshopper."Good morning, Grasshopper! What should we play today?"And the butterfly and the grasshopper played all day long.

The butterfly and the grasshopper saw the ant passing by with its heavy load."Grasshopper, look at Ant. He works and works every day without rest. Even when there is so much to eat," said the butterfly, laughing."Really! Oh, poor silly Ant!" answered Grasshopper, also laughing.

A week later, it began to rain. It was a typhoon, and the torrents of rain caused great flooding. None of the insects could go out to find food. But the ant family had stored a lot of food,so they did not need to go outside in the rain to find more.Suddenly, the wind blew the ant’s window wide open. When he got up to close it, the ant was surprised at what he saw. Butterfly and Grasshopper were there in the rain, outside the window."Butterfly, Grasshopper! Where are you going? The typhoon is too strong and dangerous.You should go home now!""We need to find something to eat because we are very hungry, Ant," answered Butterfly, shivering."No! Butterfly, you need to go home now! It’s very dangerous!" shouted Ant.But Butterfly and his friend Grasshopper had no choice but to try to find food outside.

The butterfly and the grasshopper fell into some water. Ant wanted to help them, but the whole village was flooded, and it was too dangerous to go out. Two hungry birds saw the butterfly and the grasshopper helpless in the water and ate them up."Oh, poor Butterfly and Grasshopper." Ant couldn’t do anything. He felt sad. Then Ant remembered what Grandfather Ant had told him when he was young."If you don’t prepare for tomorrow, there will be no tomorrow. So always work hard."Ant closed his eyes and prayed for Butterfly and Grasshopper."Help! Help!"

"If you don’t prepare for tomorrow, there will be no tomorrow, so always work hard" is something that children are always reminded of in the Philippines.The Philippine proverb, "If you put something away now, then you will have something later" is similar to the Korean saying "There is no winter for those who do not prepare in summer."

Since I was young, I have loved to participate in poetry,speech, essay, storytelling, and fairy tale competitions. Eventhough my Korean is not good, I have been active in thethings I like. I tell Koreans about my culture and customsthrough multicultural, bilingual lectures and storytellingand translating. Through this Multi-value, Multi-togetherChildren’s Book Contest, I have had the chance to dosomething fun with a children‘s book. I chose a famous storyfrom the Philippines called, ‘The Ant and the Butterfly’

Scientists are still using their knowledge, wisdom and advanced technology to search for another "Earth" in the universe where humans can live. There are too many planets in the universe to count. But surprisingly, only the Earth is uninhabitable for humans. This fact gives us special impressions and enlightenment. I am even more impressed with those women from other countries who came to Korea to work together to write. We live in one world. We are a "global family" from many countries. A family must trust each other, rely on each other, and care for each other. A family should offer a hug first, smile first, and give kindness first. A family must be together in pain, overcome suffering together, and walk together. I admire all those who wrote great stories in these "Multi-value, Multi-together" children’s books. Because all of them, despite being tired from working, child-rearing, housekeeping, and caring for the elderly, were still able to finish their work. And it must have been even more difficult for them to write in Korean. But then, it is an astonishing power they have, that writing one time can’t compare to speaking hundred times. The power to express one’s thoughts more clearly.The power to communicate more politely with other people. The power to educate their children more fairly. They have this power.I recommend that this project should be continued in the future, giving pride and hope to many immigrant women and their families. Kyung-sil Roh Writer

title: Strong Like Mom
content:
“Come on, Naning! Keep pulling!” shouted Naning’s friends. It was Naning’s turn to pull the coconut leaf. But, no matter how hard Naning pulled, the leaf didn’t move. “I give up. I can’t go on. I want to go home,” said Naning.

Naning wanted to be strong like Mom. Mom could lift, pull, or even push heavy objects with ease. Mom said drinking an herbal drink could make you stronger. Naning grabbed a bottle of herbal drink. However, she couldn’t even open the cap. “Here let me help,” said Mom.

With a single twist, the bottle opened. Mom really was strong. “Naning, you’re free tomorrow, right? Come fishing with me,” suggested Mom. Naning couldn’t wait! She had already heard of Mom’s greatness at sea. Now Naning could see it for himself.

Before dawn, Naning and Mom were already at the boat. “I brought boots and a change of clothes for you. I also brought a small net. You can learn how to fish using a big net later,” Mom said. Naning wore her boots. She felt just like Mom, how great! Naning and Mom were ready to set sail.

“Let me try to turn on the engine Mom,” Naning said. She had once seen Mom do it. Ugh, turns out that cranking the engine wasn’t easy.

“Let’s crank it together,” said Mom. “One, two, and three!” they counted. Vrooom! The engine roared to life and the boat headed out toward the sea. “Please help me get rid of the water that enters the boat later, okay,” said Mom.

Getting rid of the water was hard. The bucket was too big, so Naning used a dipper instead. Not to mention, a bucket full of water was heavy. On top of that, Naning’s hair kept falling across her eyes.

Naning’s eyes were stinging from sweat. “If I was Mom, what would I do?” she thought.

“Oh yeah. I should wear a head cover just like Mom,” Naning decided. Now neither hair nor sweat would bother her.

“Here’s the place,” said Mom while pointing toward the flying birds. Naning understood what Mom meant. Birds could be a sign that there were lots of fish in the area. Mom threw her net, and so did Naning.

The sun was blinding Naning. She couldn’t see well. She looked at Mom again. “If I was Mom, what would I do?” Naning thought.

Naning needed to wear a hat just like Mom. A cone hat would do. Now she was no longer blinded by the sun. Naning threw her net carefully.

Now, Naning and Mom had to wait. The sun’s rays made Naning thirsty. “Let’s drink some water,” Mom suggested. After drinking some water, Naning felt refreshed.

Come on, it’s time to pull the net,” said Mom. Naning pulled her net. “Yikes, it’s so heavy!” she exclaimed. “This is heavier than the bucket.”

With all her strength, Naning pulled the net again. Slowly the net began to rise. There were several fish on the net. Hooray!

“Let’s try throwing our nets near the coral,” said Mom while steering the boat. “If we’re lucky, we can catch a lobster.”

Mom threw her net again. This time Mom struggled to lift her net. “Looks like we got a lot of fish. The net is really heavy,” said Mom.

“Come help me lift it up,” urged Mom. Why did Mom need Naning’s help? Wasn’t Mom usually strong? Surprised, Naning helped Mom. “One, two, three, pull!” they said in unison.

As the boat neared the docks, Naning was still thinking. Why did Mom ask for her help? “Let’s eat lunch, Naning,” Mom called out. Yum, tiwul rice and salted fish tasted very good.

After lunch was finished, Naning felt more energetic. “Wow, we caught way more fish than usual,” Mom noticed. Mom separated the fish from the net. Naning placed the fish in a box.

“Oh this is so heavy,” Mom groaned as she lifted the box of fish. Again, Mom needed Naning’s help.

Mom and Naning lifted the box together. “One, two, three, lift!” they said. The box was still heavy even though they were both lifting it. Mom and Naning had to take breaks every now and then.

“We’re there!” exclaimed Naning, panting. Mom stroked Naning’s head and said, “Thank you Naning. You were really strong today. You made my job easier.” Naning smiled. Turns out she could be as strong as Mom.

title: Dog Makes a Mess
content:
Every day, Lulu the dog took a walk in the park. She loved to see the perfect green grass.

One day, she smelled something delicious coming from an overflowing garbage can. She ran over to investigate.

When she tried to climb inside, the can fell over! “Oops! What a mess,” she said. “But now I can find out what that yummy smell is. I’m hungry!”

As Lulu continued to dig in the can, the trash spread all through the park and over the green grass.

At last, Lulu found the source of the delicious smell. It was coming from inside a shiny black bag. I can’t wait for a snack,” she said. “I wonder what’s inside?”

But before Lulu could take a bite, someone began shouting at her. “Hey you over there! You’re kicking trash all over my beautiful hair!” It was the grass! Her name was Sasha, and she loved to keep her green hair clean and perfect. But now it was filthy. Lulu was too hungry to notice. She tore open the shiny bag and dug into the food inside.

After licking the containers clean, Lulu kicked them to the side. Plastic bags got stuck in Sasha’s hair. Banana peels tumbled past her roots. And a dirty box flew into her face. “What are you doing?” Sasha yelled. “Don’t you realize what a mess you are making? You are ruining my hair!”

But Lulu still did not hear Sasha’s protests.

Finally, Lulu had her fill and lay down for a nap. But while she was resting, the wind blew a plastic bag onto a fire ant nest. The ants were curious, and some of them crawled into the bag.

When the wind picked up again, it carried the bag and the ants high into the air.

At last the bag came down, but it landed on Lulu’s face! The ants were startled and began to bite Lulu. It really hurt!

Lulu rolled around, trying to get the bag off her nose. Sasha saw Lulu struggling, and called out to her, “Come here! I will help you!”

Lulu stumbled over to Sasha. When she rubbed her head on Sasha’s soft green hair, the bag finally came off.

Lulu was badly hurt, but she was very grateful to the grass for helping her. “How can I repay you for your kindness?” she asked.

“Everyone comes to the park to play on beautiful green grass. But now I am so dirty that no one will come. Please clean me up and take care of the park so everyone can enjoy coming here!”

Lulu was happy to help her new friend. She cleaned up all the trash and helped Sasha wash her hair. Now, the grass was beautiful again and they could enjoy the park together!

title: Where the River Monster Roams
content:
"Look, it’s the monster!"Somenea rushed to the edge of the school yard. "Where?"Somenea’s friend Sokhom turned around with a smirk. "Too bad, Somenea, it just disappeared into the water. It was the coolest thing I’ve ever seen."

Somenea had been waiting weeks to see the monster. Ever since Keo’s dad saw something strange by the river, the monster was all the kids at school could talk about.Somenea had even set up a lookout in her yard. It had everything: a blanket to cover her, a place for snacks, and most importantly, a net to throw on the monster!And now she had missed her chance!

"What’s all this talk of monsters?" asked Teacher Chey."We just saw a monster in the river, it was a baby Godzilla!" Sokhom said. "It had skin that looked like armor and bony plates on its back!" "Really?" Teacher Chey said excitedly. "That sounds like the Siamese crocodile that people have been talking about.""I’m not afraid of Siamese monsters, I’ll protect the school!" Somenea said, swinging her arms around wildly like swords."No, Somenea. Siamese crocodiles. They’re very rare animals," said Teacher Chey."My friend is visiting the area to look for them. She’s a wildlife research specialist. She’ll be excited to hear about this."

The next day, Teacher Chey introduced his friend, Ms. Sett, to the class.Somenea’s arm immediately shot up and she asked, "Do you chase monsters?""No, I don’t chase monsters," Ms. Sett said with a smile. "I am looking for crocodiles though, and crocodiles are descendants of dinosaurs, so you could say I’m looking for dinosaurs."

Somenea thought dinosaur hunting sounded like a great adventure. When she saw Ms. Sett outside the school after class, she ran right up to her."Can I help you look for the crocodile?" she asked, tugging at her arm. "I’ve already set up a monster . . . I mean dinosaur lookout at home."

"Sure!" said Ms. Sett, as she set down her map of the area. "The more information we have about how the Siamese crocodile lives, the more we’ll be able to do to save it from extinction.""Extinction?" Somenea asked. "What’s that?" "It’s when there are no more of an animal anywhere in the world," replied Ms. Sett."Oh, wow. That’s sad. We need to help them," Somenea said."Do you think you could build one of your amazing crocodile-spotting forts here, by the fence?""Definitely," said Somenea. "I’ll build the best lookout ever.""We call those lookouts blinds," said Ms. Sett. "They help us observe animals without being seen by them."

Sokhom and Keo helped Somenea build a crocodile blind in the corner of the school. Teacher Socheata even gave them a cover for it. "This looks great, team!" said Ms. Sett.

"I found a net," said Somenea. "So we can throw it on the Siamese crocodile and capture it! We’ll be heroes!""If you’re going to be my wildlife research assistant, you won’t be catching any crocodiles," Ms. Sett said.Somenea was surprised. "Why not?" she asked.

"Our job is to observe animals, that just means to look at them and understand their lives. We want to know what they eat, where they travel, and how many there are.""So you’re only learning about the animals?" Somenea said. "Can’t you just read a book?"That’s a great question!" Ms. Sett said. "We’re learning specifically about what they do here, in this location. We also take notes on the other animals we see, since they might have an effect on the crocodiles.Then we can help your community make good decisions about how to best protect the animals, ourselves, and our resources."

"How will we know when to look for the Siamese crocodile from our fort?" asked Somenea."We won’t," responded Ms. Sett. "That’s the hard part but also the fun part of being a wildlife researcher. We often spend weeks looking for animals. You’ll need to watch the river as much as possible. I’ll stop by in a few days to see what you’ve found. Good luck!"Somenea asked students and teachers for their help, and for the next week they all took turns, from sunrise to sunset, looking for animals from the blind.

They wrote down the animals they saw, when they saw them, and what they were doing.The list of animals grew longer each day. Some students even saw the Siamese crocodile, including Sokhom. He made sure to remind Somenea that he’d seen it twice now.But it never showed up when Somenea was watching.

On the day that Ms. Sett was set to return, Somenea and her mother got up early to take a turn on the sunrise watch at the blind. Somenea looked out at the river but only saw a small odd looking piece of wood drifting in the water. Then the piece of wood turned.

"Wait!" exclaimed Somenea. "Is that the crocodile?"The piece of wood began to rise out of the water. It was the crocodile’s head! Somenea could now see the distinct bony plates on its back."It is! It’s the Siamese crocodile!" she whispered excitedly.

Later that day, Somenea was eager to share her notes with Ms. Sett. "We saw so many animals. And the best part . . . we saw the Siamese crocodile five times!"

"That’s wonderful, Somenea," Ms. Sett said. "My research team also saw the Siamese crocodile up river. That means that there is enough food and places for the Siamese crocodile to live here. Thanks to your research, we might be able to introduce Siamese crocodiles back into this area and help save them."

Somenea and Ms. Sett presented the results of their research to the town and mayor the next evening. People were excited that they could be part of helping to save the Siamese crocodile.

Even Sokhom was impressed. "You make a pretty good dinosaur hunter!" he said with a grin. "Hopefully we can see more of them now.""You did a great job, Somenea," Ms. Sett added. "You can be part of my research team anytime!"

title: Who Will Win?
content:
This is the Shapes Family. Today, the Lantern Competition was announced in their town.

The Shapes get ready for the competition.

Circle got to work. But, he wouldn’t let his little sister Triangle help him.

Ms. Rectangle said to her, "Make a lantern with triangles!"

Circle made a lantern with circles. He showed it to Mr. Square. Triangle made a lantern with triangles.

"Don’t you think we are using the same old shapes?" asked Circle. Triangle agreed.

Together, they made a new lantern with circles and triangles.

Mr. Square made a lantern with squares. The Shapes finished making their lanterns.

The winning lantern design was announced.

It was the circle-triangle lantern!

title: Gold Shoes
content:
For my birthday Dida gave me gold shoes.

In the card she wrote: “These are magic shoes. They are made of jute, the golden grass that grows in your motherland. They will take you where you want to go and always bring you home. And, wherever you may go, you will leave a beautiful footprint.”

I did not like the shoes. They were not colorful and did not make me any taller. The other kids had shoes with lights and bounce. I had jute shoes.

But then one day, walking home from school, I lost my way and had to turn back. As I walked, I saw my footprints on the road, leading me back to where I had taken the wrong turn.

My footprint was a little house with flowers all around. I understood why Grandma gave me these shoes as a gift! My shoes have beautiful soles and they will always take me home. I love my gold walking shoes!

NoteOur earth gives us everything we need to live - water, food, air, and materials to make clothes and homes. Jute, known as the Gold of Bengal, has a very small carbon footprint and can be used to make absolutely anything from shoes to boats to tea.

title: No Ordinary Herbs
content:
Jingle, jangle! Every time Tinuk saw children riding their bikes to school, she got more excited about saving up money. She wanted to have a bike like theirs. In a year, Tinuk would study at a junior high school that was quite far from her house. It would be easier for her to ride a bicycle there. Hopefully Mom could give Tinuk more pocket money.

However, this afternoon Mom came home with a lot of leftover herbal drinks. Oh no, Mom would be at a loss if she couldn’t sell all her herbal drinks. She wouldn’t have any extra pocket money to give Tinuk. Hmm, maybe Tinuk could help her out.

Tinuk decided to bring the herbal drinks with her to the field. She would sell the herbs to her friends before they played football. Tinuk needed to move the herbal drink bottles out of the basket. She couldn’t carry the basket like Mom could.

“Get your herbal drinks here! Herbs for a healthy body,” Tinuk announced. Tinuk’s friends came up to her. However, they didn’t like herbal drinks that taste bitter. They only wanted sweet herbs. One friend even jokingly asked for a strawberry-flavored one. Hearing that, an idea popped into Tinuk’s head.

Tinuk would make different flavored herbal drinks. Most importantly, they must all be sweet. Tinuk added a lot of cinnamon to the turmeric mix, but…

Yuck! It tasted bitter and smelled strange. There wasn’t even a bit of sweetness to it. It turns out that cinnamon isn’t sweet after all. Maybe the measurements needed to be changed? Tinuk mixed in other fragrant ingredients like lemongrass, ginger, and pandan.

Why is the kitchen such a mess?” Mother asked. “I’m making herbal drinks, Mom,” answered Tinuk. “Have a taste.”

“What kind of herb is this? It’s too fragrant and too sweet.” Mother wrinkled her nose. “It’s rice with aromatic ginger. I mixed in a lot of pandan leaves, so it smells good,” Tinuk answered.

Hmm, that meant Tinuk used too much sugar and pandan. She needed to try other flavor combinations.

However, there was only a little bit of sugar and cinnamon left. Tinuk felt guilty. Mom must not have much money left to buy more herbal ingredients. Tinuk would use some of her own savings to buy more brown sugar and cinnamon.

While waiting in line at the stall, Tinuk saw a shelf filled with various packaged herbs. There was even a picture of a woman who resembled Mom on the packaging. How interesting.

Wow, so many people were buying this drink. Was it because it’s sold in a small bottle? The small picture and name of the drink written on the bottle made it even more interesting. Another new idea popped into Tinuk’s head.

As soon as she got home, Tinuk immediately looked for small bottles. However, she could only find her water bottle.

Tinuk used her savings again to buy plastic bottles. She didn’t mind, as long as more people would buy Mom’s herbal drinks.

Now was time for Tinuk to draw a picture for the bottle. What should she draw? Tinuk wasn’t good at drawing Mom. Oh, she just thought of something. Tinuk would draw Mom’s silhouette instead. Underneath, she wrote down a phone number and the brand name. Tinuk gave it the name Mrs. Marni’s Herbal Drinks. That way people would know that these were the same herbal drinks her mom usually carried around.

Tinuk then photocopied the logo at a photocopy store. She cut out the logos and stuck them on to the bottles, but she wasn’t done yet. There was something else Tinuk needed to do.

Tinuk needed to make a sign to put up in front of her house. Again, Tinuk used her savings to buy cardboard paper and colored markers.

Instead of saving up her money, she had ended up spending more. Tinuk must try her best to make this work.

There was only one more thing left to do. Tinuk had to promote Mom’s herbal drinks so that more people would buy it. They needed to know that Mom’s herbal drinks now come in branded bottles. “If you want to order herbal drinks, you can contact this number,” Tinuk said as she handed out fliers.

"Can I have a bottle of herbs?” Hurray! The first customers had arrived.

More and more customers were right behind them. Not only did Mom’s herbal concoctions sell, but Tinuk’s did too. “Can I order some over the phone to send to a friend?” someone asked. Of course!

Almost every day, Tinuk added more money into her savings. Before she knew it, she had saved up enough money to buy a bike!

“You can borrow my bike to sell your herbs, Mom,” Tinuk smiled.

title: Riding the Horse Cart
content:
"Riding a horse cart to Tanang River…"Grandpa sings as he wipes Rio's horse cart toy.

"When will we ride a horse cart, Grandpa?" Rio asks.

"Well, we need to go to Bukittinggi city to ride it. Horse carts are hard to find in this city now," Grandpa answers.

"Let's go to Bukittinggi and use my savings to pay for the cart ride!"Grandpa laughs. "Keep your savings for later, Rio. Let's just go there. I miss that city anyway."

"Riding the horse cart in Bukittinggi…" Rio imitates the song Grandpa sang.

They arrive in Bukittinggi, and Rio is excited!

The last time they were in the city, they didn't get to ride in a horse cart. This time, Rio gets to sit in the front seat of the horse cart with the driver!

Rio even gets to hold the horse reins.

"Rio, let's play I Spy. You guess what I am seeing, okay?" Grandpa says.

"I spy a circle and four triangles. It is something that reaches high up in the sky."

"It's the Gadang Clock!" Rio shouts.

"One more! I spy a giant green wall. A river flows beneath it;Mount Singgalang is behind it."

"It's Sianok Cliff! That's too easy, Grandpa!" Rio replies.

Grandpa laughs. "Try this one. Its mouth is a half circle. Its body is long and winding. It spans through time and ages."

"Hmm…the Japanese Cave?"

"Wow, you are smart!" Grandpa says.

"Now it's your turn to give me riddles!" Grandpa tells Rio.

"I spy something white and tender, dressed with yummy, sweet brown sauce…"

"Ampiang dadiah!" Grandpa answers. "Haha…are you starving, Rio?"Together, they get off the cart and go into the nearby market.

Having answered all of Grandpa's riddles correctly, Rio gets his favorite snacks: fermented buffalo milk in a brown sugar sauce, and mixed fruit covered with shaved ice.This trip to the city was fun and delicious!

title: Small Lights
content:
Thida and her father were traveling to visit her grandpa in the countryside.

Thida thought the countryside was boring. It was very dark at night.

When they arrived, Thida asked her grandpa if she could watch TV. "We don’t have TV here," he replied, "But you could join the children playing nearby!"

Thida was impressed with how high the kids could fly their kites. One boy asked if she wanted to join them. She felt shy and just shook her head.

But when the boy put his kite away, Thida took it for herself.

Thida tried to get the kite to fly. She tossed it in the air, and she dragged the string while walking backwards. But she could not get the kite to go up!

Finally, a strong wind began to blow, and the kite flew into the air! But after a moment, the string snapped and the kite drifted away.

The boy saw his kite floating away and ran up to Thida. "What did you do with my kite? I want it back!""I am sorry," Thida replied. "I didn’t mean to lose it." "My name is Dara. Will you come with me to look for it?" the boy asked.

"Why don’t you just buy a new one?" Thida asked. "Because I made it with my grandpa!"

Dara explained how his grandfather had taught him to use paper, string, and scissors to make the kite.

Thida noticed the sun was beginning to set."How will we find the kite in the dark? There are no lights here like in the city." "There are other kinds of lights here in the country," Dara replied.

Together, Thida and Dara went looking for the kite.

Just as the sun went down, Thida found the kite!

As the sky grew dark, Thida saw small, blinking lights all around her. "What are those cool little lights?" she asked Dara. "Those are fireflies! They are our country lights!" Dara explained.

When she got back to her grandpa’s house, Thida couldn’t wait to tell him about her adventures in the countryside and her new friend!

title: The Blind Termites
content:
Every morning the hazel ants led the herd of termites to the green plants. The termites drank from tasty, juicy plants until they were full. So the termites showed gratitude to the ants day and night.

These termites were blind, and without the ants they couldn't reach the plants and quench their thirst.

The hazel ants also protected the termites from ladybugs. The termites had short wings. They wouldn't be able to fly away from the ladybugs if they attacked. So the termites showed gratitude to the ants day and night.

The ants were also responsible for the termites’ eggs. The ants carried the eggs for the termites, and hid them underground. When the eggs hatched, they led them to feed on the roots of the juicy plants. So the termites showed gratitude to the ants day and night.

One day, while the ants were carrying the eggs to place them underground, one of the eggs fell and rolled away. The ants didn't notice the missing egg and went on their way. The egg ended up on a small leaf and hatched after a few days.

When Terry the Termite was born, she opened her eyes and looked around. She was astounded by the beauty of nature around her. She drank from the juicy plants until she quenched her thirst. She liked the taste of the juice and drank it every day. Terry grew large and healthy.

One day a lady bug attacked! Terry saw her coming, so she flapped her wings and flew away. She flew all the way to the field where the termites lived with the hazel ants.

"Those insects look just like me! I will go say hello." She flew over to meet the termites in the field. "Hello there! You look just like me," she said. "Maybe we are related!"When they heard Terry's voice and her wings flapping, they were astonished. "Who are you? How can you fly?" they asked. Terry was surprised to realize they could not see nor fly, like she could.

Terry looked around and saw other termites drinking juice the ants prepared for them. She saw ants carrying the termite eggs away and wondered where they took the eggs.

Terry decided to follow them. She saw the eggs hatch. Tiny termites came out. Ants kept them in holes until they became poor sighted, then they cut their wings.

Terry hurried to tell the other termites what she had seen. The termites could not believe it. "That’s not true!" they cried. "The ants feed us and protect us." "But look at me!" Terry begged. "Why do you think I can fly and see? Because I didn’t grow up with the ants."

An old termite spoke up. "Even if you are right, why should we change things if the ants bring us food and protect us from the ladybugs?" Then she looked at the rest of the termites and said, "Let’s go. It’s time to show our gratitude to the ants."

But Terry would not give up. "Have any of you seen the warm rays of the sun through the leaves of trees?" she asked. "Have any of you seen the waterfall as it flows between the rocks in the river? Or the wonder of two cuddled clouds under moonlight? There is life beyond the field. If you had your wings, you could fly and hide from ladybugs, without needing anyone to protect you."

No one cared what Terry said. Only three termites decided to stay with her. They hid together behind the leaves until the ants passed by.

Terry protected her friends. She told them when she saw danger. She also told them about the wonderful colors she could see.

Before winter, the termites laid lots of eggs. Terry hid them under the roots of a plant, where the ants could not find them. It was the beginning of new generation of termites.

When spring arrived, the eggs hatched. The baby termites gazed at the wonder of nature. They played together and ate and drank from many delicious plants.

While they wandered around, the young termites saw a field of insects and hazel ants. The little ones approached and said, "You look like us!" They managed to convince twenty more termites to leave the field and the ants. They protected them and told them about the beauty of everything they could see.

THE END

title: Where Did My Home Go?
content:
One morning near the river bank, Witty Turtle woke up under her favorite coconut tree. Witty began her daily morning exercise, going in and out, in and out of her cozy carapace.

Then, Witty sat down to relax. But, suddenly . . .

. . . a coconut fell and knocked Witty right out of her shell! She felt dizzy and confused. "Where am I? Where has my carapace gone?" she said as she looked around.

Without her shell, Witty would be cold and unprotected. She must find it! "I will look everywhere until I find my carapace," she said.

Witty walked along the edge of the river to look in the mud and sand. Soon, she found a hard round shell. She knocked on it and said, "Are you my carapace?"

The ball uncurled into an angry armadillo! "No, this is my home. I curl up inside it to hide from cold and predators." "Yes, I see," Witty said. "My home cannot roll into a ball. My scales are made of hard rings that show how much I have grown each season."

Witty continued searching and soon found another hard shell. She knocked and said, "Are you my carapace?"

A quiet voice whispered, "No, this is my shell." Then a snail poked its head out. "The strong shape holds my body in place, as I have no bones."

"Yes, I see," said Witty. "My shell is not a spiral shape like yours. It has a top and bottom that form around my bones."

Next, Witty Turtle searched for her carapace in the river. But the water was strong and pushed her over onto her back!

Finally, she managed to turn over and swim down under the water. Soon, she saw a hard shell on the bottom. She knocked and said, "Are you my carapace? "A deep voice growled, "No, I am an oyster. I open my shell to eat and close it to hide from predators."

'Yes, I see," Witty said, "I can go in and out of my carapace, but it does not close up tight!"

Witty Turtle didn’t give up. Every time she found a new shell, she knocked and asked if it was her carapace. But each one turned out to be the home of another animal.

Suddenly, Witty saw a dark shadow moving towards her. An alligator! She quickly hid behind a rock. If an alligator found her without her shell, she would become its dinner in a moment!

After the alligator swam away, Witty raced to the surface and swam to the shore as fast as she could.

Witty returned to her coconut tree, afraid she may have lost her cozy home forever. But then . . .

BOOOOM!!! Something fell and landed on her head.

It was her carapace! "Yes, this is it! My carapace has rings that show how I've grown each season, a hard top and bottom to protect me, and comfortable holes for my head and legs to poke in and out. I am so happy to be home!"

That night, Witty Turtle went to sleep under her favorite coconut tree, safe and warm at last.

THE END

title: When is Mom Coming Home?
content:
Mom was going to Jakarta to work as a babysitter. While Mom was away, Alia and Bagas were staying with Mbah Kung, their grandfather. Alia was nervous, but she was also excited. *Mbah in the Javanese language means grandpa or grandma.

“How fun, we can play all afternoon. No one’s going to tell us to come home!” said Bagas. But Mbah Kung came to pick them up. They had to stop playing and go home at once. After only one day, Alia missed Mom.

Alia and Bagas had to get up early, even on the weekends. “Help me sweep the yard! Weekends are no excuse to be lazy,” Mbah Kung scolded.

Mbah Kung even made them take baths on the weekend. “Do we really have to take a bath?” Alia grumbled. Mom used to brush Alia’s hair and put it up with pins or ribbons. Now, Alia had to do all that herself. What a hassle!

“Come here, let me help you!” Mbah Kung said. Alia did as she was told. “But why is one of my pigtails higher than the other?” Alia complained. But Mbah Kung told her not to fuss over such small matters. Alia was upset! This made her miss Mom even more.

When Alia and Bagas climbed the guava tree, Mbah Kung scolded, “Hey, get down from there! You’ll fall!” “Don’t do this, don’t do that,” Alia mocked.

When it was time for lunch Mbah Kung cooked the same meal every day. Either vegetables with peanut sauce, stir fry, or vegetable stew. “Just eat, don’t be picky!” Mbah Kung said. Today, Alia and Bagas didn’t want to eat. When Mbah Kung went back to his room, they took their bikes and left.

They saw their neighbor Mbah Tum drying grain. Her movements made it seem like she was playing a game. Alia and Bagas wanted to try for themselves. “Even it out, back and forth!” Alia instructed Bagas.

However, Mbah Kung came to pick them up. “Why haven’t you two eaten? Eat first, then you can play!” Mbah Kung ordered. Alia and Bagas reluctantly went back home.

“I’m bored of eating vegetables and peanut sauce,” Bagas whispered. “Let’s cook for ourselves. We’ll put some vegetables in eggs, just like Mom does,” Alia said. “Yes!” Bagas agreed.

Alia prepared the ingredients. She peeled garlic and cut up vegetables. She ground some pepper. She added the vegetables to the eggs and mixed them together. She had just started to fry the egg batter, when Bagas called for her.

Bagas’ bicycle chain had come off. Alia helped him fix it. Suddenly, a strange smell wafted through the air. “Oh, no!’ Alia shrieked.

“The eggs are scorched!” Alia cried.

“The heat was too high! Never leave the stove when you’re cooking, it’s dangerous!” Mbah Kung scolded again. “What were you trying to make?” “Vegetable omelettes,” Alia answered. “I don’t want to eat vegetables with peanut sauce anymore,” Bagas added. Mbah Kung sighed and invited Alia to cook with him.

“Slice the carrots to the shape of matches,” ordered Mbah Kung. “Round cuts also work!” Alia said. “The garlic should be grounded,” Mbah Kung suggested. “Slicing them is easier,” said Alia. Alia and Mbah Kung kept arguing.

Finally, the vegetable omelettes were ready to be served. Would it taste like Mom’s cooking? “Bagas, let’s dig in!” Alia called. However, Bagas was nowhere to be seen.

“Bagas must have run away because you’re so strict, Mbah Kung,” said Alia quietly. Mbah Kung didn’t say anything.

Ring, ring! Bagas was back. “Are the omelettes ready? I don’t like hearing you two argue,” Bagas said.

Alia brought Bagas to the table to eat. But where was Mbah Kung? Why wasn’t he eating with them?

Alia went to look for Mbah Kung in his room. Mbah Kung was looking at a photo of Mom. His eyes were full of tears. It turns out that Alia wasn’t the only one who missed Mom.

They ate together in silence. “We all miss your mom’s cooking,” said Mbah Kung. “Yes. I miss when Mom reads to me, too,” Bagas added.

Mbah Kung read them stories. Mbah Kung brushed Alia’s hair. Mbah Kung also asked them to cook with him.​

When would Mom come home? She’d be happy to see that Alia and Bagas made a new friend, Mbah Kung.

title: Disgusting!
content:
One morning, a white rabbit came into the garden to eat vegetables. Wow, these vegetables are big and green! They must be delicious! he said to himself.

But when the rabbit was about to pull a vegetable out of the ground, he saw a worm attached to the roots. "What are you doing here?" he exclaimed. "You’re covered in dirt. You’ll mess up my delicious vegetables! Go away!"

The worm tried to wiggle away...

But he did not move fast enough for the rabbit. Impatient, the rabbit grabbed a stick and poked at the worm."You go away!" he said again.

With the worm gone, the rabbit enjoyed his meal.

The next day, the vegetables were brown and wilted.What happened? he wondered. They don’t look appetizing, even though I am so hungry.

The rabbit hopped to the next farm. There he saw a bounty of fresh vegetables. These vegetables are big and fresh, he said to himself. They look delicious!

But the worm was there, too. "Ah, it’s you again!" the rabbit said. "What are you doing here?"

"I am making these vegetables fresh and healthy," the worm said.

The rabbit thought about the brown and wilted vegetables at the other farm. "So you were also making my vegetables fresh?""That’s right!" the worm replied.

"I was helping you. But you shooed me away so rudely. You were mean!"

The worm dove back beneath the dirt.

The rabbit regretted what he had done to the worm.He waited for the worm to reappear.

Finally, the worm peaked its head above the soil."I can’t stay out in the sun for too long, it’s too hot. It’s cooler down there."

The rabbit was so happy to see the worm again."Let me give you some shade from the sun!"

The rabbit was hungry and its stomach was growling. They looked at each other and laughed.

title: Nima’s First Day of School
content:
Nima is not happy today. Father buys her a pair of shoes. But she is still not happy.

Mother buys her a bag. But she is still not happy.

Nima is going to school today. But she does not want to go! Sister gives her an exercise book. But Nima still doesn’t want to go to school.

Brother brings her a book. But she is not happy. "I won’t go to school," Nima cries. Mother and father laugh.

Her parents take her to school. Nima walks as slowly as she can.

"It’s only for today. I won’t go tomorrow," Nima thinks as she walks.

At school, there are so many new friends. Now Nima is happy. She wants to go to school every day!

title: Mahatma Gandhi: The Salt March
content:
While the author, illustrator, and publisher of this book encourage and support translation of this work into other languages, they request that substantive changes to the text and art be kept to a minimum.

Many years ago, the government of Great Britain took control over the country of India.

The British made it illegal for Indians to collect, produce, or sell salt. They also forced Indians to pay a salt tax. This harmed the people of India for many years. Salt became very expensive and it was difficult for Indians, especially poor people, to buy the salt they needed.

Anyone who produced or sold salt in India, except for the British, could be imprisoned for six months.

The Indian leader Gandhi, and many others, said the salt tax and the restrictions on salt production were unfair. They decided to protest against them. Gandhi said, "Next to air and water, salt is perhaps the greatest necessity of life."

Salt is important because it makes food taste good, but more importantly, salt is essential for health.

In 1930, Gandhi organized a march from the Gandhi Ashram in Ahmedabad, to the seaside village of Dandi, in the south of Gujarat. It started with just seventy-eight people.

The marchers were called freedom fighters because they struggled not only against unfair laws but for Indian freedom from British rule.

Along the two hundred and forty miles from Ahmedabad to Dandi, thousands of people from all over India joined the march. They protested British rule, the high salt taxes, and the unfairness of not being allowed to produce and sell their own salt.

Gandhi and his followers walked about twelve miles a day and reached Dandi in three weeks. He called it "a battle of right against might."

At the end of the march, Gandhi picked up some grains of salt from the seashore and made a pledge: "With these crystals of salt, I am going to shake the foundation of the British Empire."

With the Salth March, Gandhi had launched the Civil Disobedience Movement against the British Empire.

Soon after, eighty thousand Indians, along with Gandhi, were jailed.

But the British administration eventually freed Gandhi and invited him to London to discuss reforms in India.

News of Gandhi's Salt March spread around the world. It proved to be a turning point in the history of India's independence movement. India finally gained independence from Britain in 1947.

With his simple act of standing up against injustice, Gandhi changed the world.

He showed that while each person might be as small and powerless as a grain of salt, if people of courage and conviction worked together, they could make an enormous difference.

title: Let’s Play Together, Dad!
content:
This corn husk can be made into a puppet.Niken loves to put on puppet shows with Dad.But ever since dad’s accident, they haven’t played with puppets.

Look, those chicks just hatched.They are so cute! Do you think they are boys or girls?

Mom can’t tell the difference.Let’s go and ask Dad!Niken loves to guess the gender of baby chickens with Dad.

"Dad. Are these boys or girls?” Niken asks.Usually Dad would tell her.This time, Dad doesn’t say a word.Niken’s heart sinks.

So instead, Niken goes to help Mom fish.These fish are to be sold at the market.

Hooray! Niken catches a huge fish.Dad also loves to guess if the fish are girls or boys.Maybe this time, Dad will tell her.

“Dad, are these fish boys or girls?”Dad only frowns.

Why isn’t Dad answering her?Is he sad?Seeing her Dad in the dumps hurts Niken’s heart.What can she do to cheer him up?

Then, Niken’s friends come over.They love putting on puppet shows with Dad.Dad was a wonderful storyteller.He could always make her friends laugh.

“Let’s put on a puppet show,” they cheer.But Dad only gazes at their corn husk puppets.Again, he says nothing.

Niken’s friends all go home.She knows that they are disappointed.

Hey, where’s Dad going?“Let me help you, Dad. Grab onto my shoulder.”Suddenly, Niken hears the sound of Dad’s stomach rumbling.Dad seems to be hungry.

Niken wants to buy Dad some weci.Dad loves to eat warm weci.“Wait here, Dad!"Weci is a popular fried Indonesian snack made with vegetables, flour, and sometimes shrimp.

Many people love warm weci.Niken has to hurry to buy some before they run out.

Niken is right.Many people are lining up to buy weci.It’s a good thing there are still plenty left for Niken.And they are still hot!

One for Niken, two for Mom, three for Dad.Dad will be so happy.If Dad is happy, maybe he will put on puppet shows with Niken again.

Niken runs back home as fast as she can.She doesn’t want Dad’s weci to get cold.

Ouch!

"Shoo! Shoo!”The chickens want some weci, too.Niken can’t shoo them away.

Niken wants to chase away the chickens.But she scraped her knee. It hurts.“No! Those are for Dad!”

“Niken, are you okay?” Dad calls.Niken is surprised to see Dad in front of her.She is even more surprised to see him smiling!

Niken is glad to see Dad happy again.Niken’s friends are also excited to put on more puppet shows with Dad.

Learn More People who have just lost a limb due to amputation will feel sadness, disappointment, and even depression. They need time to adapt to their new bodies. Support and trust from their families is needed to help them recover fully.

title: Uh Oh, Pang Pang Is Up to Something
content:
BANGBANG, POW, BOOMWHOOSH, POP!Who's making all that noise?It's probably pang pang again. He's always up to something.

Alright, Just a pinch of this white flour, some water, and boil it all together. Abracadabra abracadabra, count to ten...done! Now I just need to pour it into this pan and light this fire...KOONG PANG KOONG PANG!

The noise startles a mother duck and her baby ducklings, who were out on a stroll.They all flee to a cave and hide.

*Eek eek! What is that noise?Is that a ghost?*The monkeys chatter as they scramble up the trees.

"Oh no, Mr. Tiger must be angry. I must leave before he gets too angry"Snakes frantically burrow into the ground, Ants scurry into their tunnels, Birds flock into the trees.

Pang Pang watches with glee as all the animals scurry away. He feels like king of the forest.With just a few ingredients, he could scare anyone.

"Grrr, I can't take this anymore! Let me just go and snatch his pot away right now!"growled Mr. Monkey. "Me neither.My baby sister ducklings are too scared to go anywhere because of that up-to-no-good- bear. We must put an end to all this." Mrs. Duck was furious.

Having had enough, the animals in the forest held a meeting to discuss what to do with Pang Pang.

The very next day, a group of baby moles dug a large hole in front of pang pang's house.

Then, everyone else got their drums, cymbals, flutes, trumpets, violins, guitars, and started to play very loudly in front of pang pang's house.

Pang pang, who couldn't concentrate, shouted from inside the house. "AAAARGJ what is all this noise about??"Pang pang burst out angrily, "AAAARGJ what is all this noise??"As soon as he stepped out, he fell straight into the hole the moles had dug. "AHHH!"

The animals cheered and jumped excitedly, "Hooray! we got him! No more of pang pang bothering us any longer. "

Now there was a wise old goat, who watched everything happen from a distance. When the cheering died down he cleared his throat and bleeted, "Everyone! Is this what you wish to be? A village that always fights with each other? Pang Pang! what do you think? Pang pang stops and thinks for a moment.

The animals approached pang pang one by one, "our kids were getting scared and couldn't sleep at night because of your tricks. the rest of us couldn't do anything without worrying. "

"And everyone look at pang pang! He's bruised all over. Does that make you feel better? Now that you got your revenge? "

If we continue to revenge one another and make ourselves uncomfortable, one day, our forest will not last. Don't you forget that. From now on, we must try to think of a better way to live peacefully together.

What do you think everyone? What do you think is the solution ?

title: A Message in the Envelope
content:
Marlina arranged her stack of envelopes.Mrs. Rini’s messages were inside.Marlina, thanks for your help.Good luck on your exam, Marlina!Set your goals as high as the stars, Marlina!Those messages made Marlina happy.She wanted to make similar envelopes. She would give them to everyone.

Today was the fifth of the month.Mom came home after helping Mrs. Rini clean her house.She brought some envelopes.Mom said, “Time to do your duty, Marlina.”“Sure, Mom!” Marlina replied happily.First she looked for her envelope.She handed the money inside to Mom.She then read the message in the envelope:Just like lime and pomegranate. Your smile is sweet, Marlina!

Distributing the envelopes with encouraging messages every month made Marlina happy.She saw every kid laugh. Some jumped up and down with joy.They were orphans, just like Marlina had been.“Envelope of the month? Hooray!”“Thank you, Marlina!”When would Marlina be able to share her own envelopes?

On the way home, a minivan passed her.“Oh, Sarah is home,” Marlina murmured.Sarah had been hospitalized since Tuesday.Marlina wanted to visit Sarah, but she was unsure about what to bring.“Ah, I’ll make an envelope! Who knows? It might cheer her up.” Marlina smiled, thinking of a plan.

Marlina took the cover off her notebook.She folded here and folded there. She pressed here and pressed there. Marlina’s first envelope was ready!“What should I put inside?”

Marlina opened her tin money box. She put some coins in the envelope. “Oh! They’re too heavy.”

Sarah loved reading poetry.Marlina tried to write something wholeheartedly.Unfortunately…“My words are not beautiful like in a poetry book.” She crumpled the paper in disappointment.

“Drawings! Sarah likes them too!” Marlina exclaimed.Unfortunately…“I want to draw Sarah’s pretty face. Why does it look like a speckled rooster?”Besides poetry and drawings, what would cheer her best friend up?

“Aha! Sarah loves flowers!”Marlina put some ashoka flowers in her envelope.“Ouch! Ants!” she shouted.Marlina changed her mind.She would not let Sarah get bitten by ants too!

While Marlina was thinking of another plan, Mom approached.“I’m going out for a while. There is a Quranic study at our neighbor’s house.”Invitation?Marlina had an idea for her envelope!

Sarah’s envelope was ready.Unexpectedly, Mom said, “Please deliver Mrs. Endang’s clothes.”Marlina nodded, a bit reluctant.To get there faster, Marline borrowed Mom’s bike. Unfortunately, its tire was leaking.

There was no other choice. Marlina would walk.The bag of clothes slipped from her arms so many times.She hoped that the envelope for Sarah was safe in her skirt pocket.When Marlina arrived at Mrs. Endang’s house, it started raining!

While taking shelter, Marlina kept thinking about the envelope.She looked at the sky, unable to do anything.“Oh no. When will the rain stop?” Marlina stomped her foot.

After falling for a long time, the rain stopped.Marlina felt excited again to deliver the envelope.Impatient, Marlina began running on the bumpy road.

“Ouch!” she cried.She slipped in a puddle.

“My envelope! Don’t get wet, please.”

Marlina continued walking.Her leg was in pain from the fall, but she didn’t think about it.The only thing she thought about was the envelope.

Marlina was anxious when Sarah answered the door.“This is for you, Sarah,” she said.

“What is it, Marlina?” asked Sarah.“I made you an envelope. I hope you like it,” said Marlina. She wondered, Would Sarah like it?

“Yes, Marlina! I like it! I accept!”

InvitationGet well soon, Sarah.Tomorrow we will play together.…♡ We’ll make mango pudding♡ and read storybooks.I am waiting for your answer.Marlina

title: Run Away to the Stars
content:
Junior couldn't wait for the sun to set so he could watch the stars through his telescope. It was his favorite thing to do each day. Sometimes, he was so excited about outer space, he forgot to do his homework. "You can't neglect your studies," his father told him. "But I don't care about math," Junior said. "What is the point of all those numbers?" "You may not understand now," his mother replied, "but math can really take you places."

Junior's other favorite thing was his socks! He liked to wear different pairs at different times of day. When he wasn't looking at the stars, he was organizing his sock collection. "You shouldn't spend all your time inside tidying socks," his grandma said. "You should go outside and play!"

Junior tried to pay attention to his homework, but he was soon distracted again by his love for the stars. "We will have to take away your astronomy books and telescope until you can improve your grades," his father said.

Junior hurried to his room and hid his socks before his grandma could take them away too. "I wish I could run away and live somewhere that I could spend my time however I want."

More than anything, Junior wished he could travel to outer space. If he could build a rocket ship, it would take him away to he stars!

Junior collected things from around his house to use. He stayed up all night working on his rocket ship. At last, it was complete!

But he didn't know how he would power the rocket. He remembered that a rocket has to blast off at 60,000 kilometers per second to escape Earth's gravity. Junior tried using all the batteries in their house to get up to speed, but nothing happened. Then he tried filling the rocket with all the fuel from their family's storage tank. But it only sputtered.

He spent all of the next day staring out the window, trying to think of a solution. At last he had an answer, thanks to the trees in his own backyard. A catapult!

His hundreds of socks would work perfectly to help fling his rocket into space. That night, Junior finished his catapult, then stepped inside and prepared for takeoff. Would it work? Three . . . two . . . one . . .

Blast off! Junior's rocket raced through the clouds and into space. He shot past the moon and headed for the stars.

It wasn't long before Junior could see a milky white spiral of stars. It was our galaxy, the Milky Way! Soon he passed Andromeda, the next galaxy after the Milky Way. Junior couldn't believe he was finally among the stars.

But suddenly, his rocket started to slow down. It was no longer traveling up, up, and away. Junior began racing down towards Earth. He closed his eyes, afraid of crashing into the ground.

When he opened his eyes, he found himself on the floor next to his bed. It was all a dream! Junior realized that it would take a lot more than watching the stars to get to outer space. He would have to learn how to power and fly a rocket ship!

Maybe doing his math homework would take him somewhere after all . . .

The End

title: Grandpa’s Fish Pond
content:
Eating grilled fish was the best part of the weekend. But, where was Grandpa? The fish pond was overflowing!

Some fish were still stuck in the pond. Eneng must catch them. "Ujang, please get the net!" Eneng exclaimed.

"Grab it yourself or wait for Grandpa," said Ujang. "I’m trying to find my sarong. I hung it out here yesterday.”

Eneng jumped into the river. Maybe she could catch the fish with her hands.

There they were! The nimble fish easily avoided Eneng’s fingers.

Aha! At last she caught a fish. However, the fish’s body was slippery and Eneng lost her grip.

Eneng couldn’t let the fish be carried away by the river water. "Ujang, help me," Eneng exclaimed. "You said you were looking for your sarong, why are you eating cherries?" Ujang just laughed.

Aha, Eneng had an idea! Swish! She managed to catch three fish at once.

Uh, oh! The fish thrashed around. One fish jumped very high.

Oh, no! The fish got away again.

Hey, what was that? A piece of cloth was drifting in the river.

It looked like the cloth was caught on something. Eneng couldn’t pull it free.

"Hahaha, are you trying to catch fish or play in the water?" said Ujang.Eneng grimaced.

"Ujang, we helped Grandpa harvest fish before, didn't we?" Eneng suddenly remembered. “The water inlet was closed and the outlet was opened. So there was very little water in the pond."

"Well, now it's the other way around. The pond water’s overflowing. It means that the drains are clogged,” said Eneng. "Maybe that cloth’s blocking it."

“Let me pull it,” said Ujang. But he didn’t succeed either.

Maybe they could pull it out together. Splash! They were both drenched

Hmmm… what could be holding the cloth in place? Eneng reached her fingers underwater. Oh, the cloth was caught in the drainage wires.

Eneng successfully removed the cloth. Water immediately gushed out from through the drain. The water in the pool began to recede.

"Grandpa!" Eneng called. She immediately recalled the entire incident to him. "All because of this cloth," said Eneng as she spread out the cloth.

Hey, that’s my sarong!” Ujang exclaimed. “Oh my gosh!” Eneng looked at Ujang in annoyance.

“Enough you two.” Eneng, your persistence and problem-solving saved me from losing all my fish. Thank you,” Grandpa smiled. “Eneng, I’m sorry I mocked you instead of helping you. This whole problem was caused by my mistake. I will be more thoughtful and responsible,” Ujang apologized. Grandpa nodded and said, “Now it’s time for us to catch some fish.”

Ah, this was what Eneng had been looking forward to. Grandpa’s grilled fish was always special.

title: Tey Tey Times 10
content:
Tey Tey is in third grade. She likes reading and social studies.

But she does NOT like math, especially multiplication tables. "Blah blah blah!" Tey Tay thinks. "It’s so boring!"

"Do you hate multiplication like I do?" Tey Tey asks her friend Som at recess."I didn’t like it at first," Som says. "But now I like it better."

"Why do I have to learn the multiplication tables?" Tey Tey asks her friend Nita. "When will I use multiplication outside of school?""Just learn the tables," Nita says. "You will be surprised at how often you use multiplication."

"Mom, did you like learning multiplication when you were in school?" Tey Tey asks her mother that night. "Yes, I studied hard, and I got really good at multiplication," her mom says. "If I didn’t know the multiplication tables, it would be hard to manage sales at my store."

Tey Tey is surprised to hear this. Perhaps multiplication is worthwhile after all. Tey Tey begins working on the tables.

Tey Tey thinks about what her mom told her about using multiplication at her store. She makes some play money using paper, scissors, and a pen. She makes paper money worth 100 riels, 500 riels, and 1,000 riels.*riel is the money of Cambodia

Tey Tey sets up a play store and invites Som over to be her customer. "Excuse me, ma’am, how much are these cakes?" Som asks. "400 riels each, sir," Tey Tey says. "How many would you like?""I would like four of them, please," Som says. "How much is that?""Hmm," Tey Tey says, scratching her head. "400 plus 400 is 800. 800 plus 400 is 1,200…"

"You know," Som says, "using multiplication would be much faster.""But I’ve only learned my tables up to 10x 10!" says Tey Tey. "I don’t know what 4 x 40 is.""Sure you do," Som says. "Just take the two zeroes away from 400. Now you have 4. So what is 4 x 4?""I know that one!" Tey Tey says. "16!""Right! Now put the two zeroes back!""16 with two zeroes is 1,600. So, 4 cakes x 400 riels = 1,600 riels!"

A little while later, Tey Tey’s friend Nita comes by and wants to play."Hello there!" she says. "I’d like 5 skewers of grilled bananas, please. How much?"Tey Tey scratches her head again and starts to use addition to find the answer. "One skewer is 500 riels plus 500 riels…"

Tey Tey exclaims, "Wait a second, let me try again!""One banana skewer is 500 riels," Tey Tey thinks to herself. "If I drop the zeroes from 500, I get 5. And 5 x 5 is 25. Now put the zeroes back and…""That will be 2,500 riels, please," Tey Tey says to Nita, happily.

Tey Tey’s Uncle Tong sees the children playing and smiles."I’d like 6 bottles of mineral water, if you please!" he calls to Tey Tey. "I’m thirsty, so please be quick about it!

"Of course, sir," Tey Tey says. "One bottle costs 600 riels. 6 x 6 = 36. So 6 bottles will cost 3,600 riels. Is that quick enough for you?"Som and Nita clap their hands and cheer. "Tey Tey," Som says, "I think you have learned that multiplication isn’t so useless after all!"

Tey Tey smiles and agrees with them. Then she calls to her mother."Mom, I need to tell you a secret!""Oh?" her mom says, leaning down. "What is it?""You were right," Tey Tey whispers. "Multiplication isn’t so bad. And I was wondering… Could I have a job in your shop one day?"

title: Let’s Have a Water Fight!
content:
The weather is so hot today.Luckily, we’re almost done making our sand houses.Just a few more touches.Suddenly....

Flood! Flood!A rush of water collapses our sand houses.Everything is ruined in a blink of an eye.

We all stand there in shock.But Alif bursts out in laughter.He is never one to say much and seldom plays with other kids.

Alif! You used up my drinking water!”“Alif, go and play over there, okay?”Alif turns away and sulks.

We go back to playing.Oh no, Alif is back.He mustn’t go near the water bottles!Where should we hide them?

Hmm... looks like this breadfruit tree will come in handy.Its branches are quite high.The water bottles will be safe up there.

The bottles sway in the wind.This makes Alif even more interested.He tries to reach for them.“Water... water...,” he calls out.

Alif and I are the same age, but Alif still acts like a child.It’s hard to understand what he wants.Maybe this time he’s really thirsty.It’s better if I just give him my water bottle.

He quickly opens the lid of the bottle.Before I can stop him, Alif pours all my water out on the ground.He jumps in the puddle happily.

My friends grumble.“Alif, you should go back home and play with water at your own house.”Alif runs away.“Mom... mom...,” he wails.

I feel guilty. I go over to Alif’s house.He is playing with water, but there is no smile on his face.It looks like playing with water alone isn’t enough to make Alif happy.He was happy earlier because he was playing with us.

Aha! I know.I invite Alif to come back and play with us.“Alif, come play over here!”-----------------Alif looks happy,--------------- but not for long.

Alif approaches us again.“Water... water...,” he giggles.“No Alif, don’t come here!” everyone shouts.

We grow quiet and stopped playing.“Let’s go home. We can play again tomorrow.”“Tomorrow we’ll have a water fight!”“That’s right. We’ll have a water fight!”We cheer.

I hurry home.I have to prepare my spray bottle.---------------- We have this water fight once a year,the day before Ramadan.

At every house, various forms of water containers are prepared.The buckets and water remind me of Alif,but he is nowhere in sight.

The water fight begins!First, we smear each other’s faces.The charcoal and ink make us unrecognizable.And then…

…it is time for the water fight!We chase and spray each other with water.There’s Alif.He can’t stop laughing.

He slowly splashes water in my direction.I spray him back as hard as I can.Alif laughs, and I do too.This is the first time we have fun together.

Now I know how to play with Alif.But, we have to wait.During Ramadan, we don’t play outside.I help Dad sell food to break our fast.

Ramadan goes by.My friends and I play together once more.Alif no longer bothers us.We have a new game to play with Alif.

Water fight!It’s fun to get wet once in a while.

Learn More Mental DisabilityIn this story, Alif has mental disabilities that affect his mental and intellectual development. Children with mental disabilities like Alif often struggle to concentrate, maintain emotional stability, and interact with other people. Water Fight Tradition Several places in Indonesia’s Java Island have water fight traditions. The day before Ramadan, locals spray each other with water. This symbolizes self-cleansing before entering the holy month of Ramadan.

title: The Torch of Mango
content:
"One evening, Ben and Bo came to Mango’s house together.""Mango, let’s go play!""Just a minute."

"It’s so dark. I’m bringing my torch with me.""Hahaha! Why would you need a torch? Girls really are scaredy-cats."

"La la la…""There’s nothing we fear!"

"Eeek, boogeyman!"

"Let’s see! Oh, it’s not a boogeyman, look, you guys!" – Mango said.

"La la la… We are as happy as a clam."

"Eep, gho… ghost!"

"Phew… It’s just a kitten."

"La la la… We sing our hearts out."

"Oh, look, there seems to be someone standing there!""Hello… mis… mister!" They all got a little nervous.

"Hihihi… They’re just some clothes.""Now you can see how useful my torch is, right?" – Mango said.

"Hehe, we boys also need a torch like you, Mango." – Ben agreed.

title: Armenians of Dhaka
content:
“Have you ever heard of the Armenians of Dhaka?” Nahian asked. Mira shook her head."The Armenians came here hundreds of years ago from a far away land called Armenia. Many of them enjoyed Bengal and they settled down and built a church which is still here today.”

“The Armenians lived in Old Dhaka, in an area called Armanitola,” Nahian continued. “They were jute and leather traders, and lived in large mansions.When one of them died, she or he was buried in the center of the neighborhood in the Armenian graveyard by the church. Today, there are over 35 0g raves there!”

“There is a road, called Armenian Street, which was a popular shopping place where all these merchants lived.”“What did they sell there?” asked curious Mira, who loved shopping. “All sorts of things.”“Biscuits?” Mira loved biscuits.“Biscuits too! The Armenians actually opened the very first supermarkets in Dhaka. One of the shopkeepers, Agaminus Catachik, gave away a big piece of his own land to build the church in 17 81 .For many generations the Armenian church was a place Armenians went to celebrate births and cry over deaths.”

"Today that area is very crowded and the church looks like a ship rising amidst the buildings. There are many mosques and temples in Old Dhaka, and people of different religions live together in harmony, like they did hundreds of years ago.”

“So where are all the Armenians today?” Mira asked. “There aren’t many left living here, but the church and the graveyard are taken care of by the relatives of the people that once lived here. The church and the neighborhood is a living memory of how different cultures can live side by side.”

NoteArmenians settled and created a colony in Dhaka in the early part of the 18 th century. It was one of the main centers of trade and business, along with Kolkata. Dhaka was famed for fine textiles like muslin and Armenians were involved in the textile business. Armenians brought many new things to Dhaka such as the horse carriage. They also set up the first grocery stores.
